title: Geometric pushouts of algebraic spaces along thickenings and affine maps
statement: Work with algebraic spaces over a scheme $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A thickening is a representable closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism on underlying spaces; closed immersions are tested after base change to schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The topology of an algebraic space is the quotient topology from a representable surjective etale scheme atlas. An affine map is representable and its scheme base changes have affine inverse images of affine opens. Let $T\to T^+$ be a thickening and $T\to S$ affine, all over $B$. There is a pushout $P=S\amalg_T T^+$ in algebraic spaces over $B$: for every algebraic space $Q/B$, maps $P\to Q$ correspond bijectively to pairs $S\to Q$, $T^+\to Q$ agreeing on $T$. The map $S\to P$ is a thickening. If $T,T^+,S$ are schemes, $P$ is their scheme pushout. For arbitrary algebraic spaces $X/S$, $Y/T^+$ and an isomorphism $\phi:X\times_S T\simeq Y\times_{T^+}T$, put $U=X\times_S T$ and identify it with $Y\times_{T^+}T$ by $\phi$. The pushout $Z=X\amalg_U Y$ has an induced map to $P$, and the canonical maps $$X\longrightarrow Z\times_P S,\qquad Y\longrightarrow Z\times_P T^+$$ are isomorphisms, identifying their restrictions over $T$ with $\phi$. No flatness or local finite presentation is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07VX, lemma-pushout-along-thickening (existence and thickening); Tag 07SY, lemma-pushout-along-thickening-schemes (agreement with scheme pushouts); Tag 07W0, lemma-equivalence-categories-spaces-over-pushout (canonical recovery of the two pieces).

proof.text: For compatible schemes, apply [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts]. Its statement gives exactly the two canonical isomorphisms $X\simeq W\times_P S$ and $Y\simeq W\times_P T^+$ for $W=X\amalg_{X\times_S T}Y$, compatible with the specified overlap. Its hypotheses are just a scheme thickening and an affine map; no flatness, finite-presentation or finite-order assumption is used. We shall use this scheme recovery in the relation construction and, finally, on a scheme cover of the desired space comparison maps.

source.place: Tag 07W0 reduction to Tag 07RV; Tag 07RV, affine calculation using Tag 07RU

proof.text: The scheme pushout $P$ is also a pushout against algebraic-space targets. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-colimit-upgrade-space-targets] to the finite span $S\leftarrow T\to T^+$. Joint surjectivity holds because $S\to P$ is a homeomorphism by [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout]. For an etale scheme $L\to P$, the canonical counit of [lem-sfb-scheme-infinitesimal-etale-patching] says exactly that $L$ is the scheme pushout of its base changes. The equivalence in that node also lifts every compatible etale triple, including every one with separated maps. These are all three hypotheses of the colimit criterion. This proves agreement with scheme pushouts and supplies the universal property needed below for targets which are spaces.

Now let the original three objects be spaces. Choose a scheme atlas $V\to S$, representable surjective etale. Set $U=V\times_S T$; representability and affineness of $T\to S$ make $U$ a scheme affine over $V$, and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes $U\to T$ surjective etale. By [lem-sfb-space-thickening-etale-scheme-equivalence] lift it to an etale scheme $U^+\to T^+$ with $U=U^+\times_{T^+}T$. This lift is surjective: the base-change thickening $U\hookrightarrow U^+$ and the original $T\hookrightarrow T^+$ identify their underlying point sets, so surjectivity of $U\to T$ gives surjectivity of $U^+\to T^+$. Form the scheme pushout $V^+=V\amalg_U U^+$ using [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout]. The thickening $V\to V^+$ and the two canonical maps have now been constructed before any space pushout is used.

Put $R_V=V\times_S V$, $R_U=U\times_T U$, and $R_+=U^+\times_{T^+}U^+$. These are schemes, since the space diagonals are representable [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Moreover $R_U\to R_+$ is a thickening and $R_U\to R_V$ is the affine base change of $T\to S$. Form the scheme pushout $R^+=R_V\amalg_{R_U}R_+$. The two projections on each of its pieces agree on $R_U$, and hence induce $s^+,t^+:R^+\rightrightarrows V^+$. For either projection the pieces $R_V\to V$ and $R_+\to U^+$ are etale and have matching pullbacks on $U$, by the fibre-product identities. Thus [lem-sfb-scheme-infinitesimal-etale-patching] makes $s^+,t^+$ etale. Step 1, applied to each projection, identifies their inverse images of $V$ with $R_V$ and of $U^+$ with $R_+$, with their canonical projections. No existence or recovery theorem for space pushouts has been used.

source.place: Tag 07VX, construction of the relation and its two etale projections

proof.text: Construct the relation operations, including the composition omitted in the source. The diagonals $V\to R_V$ and $U^+\to R_+$ agree on $U$ and therefore glue to $e:V^+\to R^+$; the flips similarly glue to $i:R^+\to R^+$. Let $K=R^+\times_{t^+,V^+,s^+}R^+$. It is etale over $V^+$ through the first source projection, by base change and composition in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. By the canonical counit of [lem-sfb-scheme-infinitesimal-etale-patching], $K$ is the scheme pushout of its restrictions to $V$ and $U^+$. Using the cartesian identifications of step 4 successively on each relation factor, these restrictions are $R_V\times_V R_V$ and $R_+\times_{U^+}R_+$; their overlap is $R_U\times_U R_U$. The usual composition maps of these three kernel relations agree on the overlap and hence glue to $c:K\to R^+$. The equations for source and target of $e,i,c$ hold because the appropriate scheme pushout determines a map by its restrictions to both pieces. This explicitly supplies all three morphisms required by [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-equivalence-relation].

source.place: Tag 07VX, omitted composition argument expanded using Tag 07RX etale counit

proof.text: For any algebraically closed field $k$ over $B$, maps from $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to a thickening factor uniquely through the closed subspace: on affine tests each element of its defining ideal is nilpotent, hence maps to zero in $k$. The scheme thickenings $V\hookrightarrow V^+$ and $R_V\hookrightarrow R^+$ therefore identify their $k$-points. The map $(s^+,t^+)$ on such points is the kernel equivalence relation $R_V(k)=V(k)\times_{S(k)}V(k)$. With the operations constructed in step 5 and the etale projections of step 4, [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-equivalence-relation] implies that $(s^+,t^+)$ is a monomorphism and an equivalence relation on all scheme tests. Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to define the algebraic space $P=V^+/R^+$ as the fppf sheafification of its orbit presheaf. It supplies a representable surjective etale atlas $V^+\to P$, its kernel pair $R^+$, and its coequalizer universal property.

source.place: Tag 07VX, equivalence relation and quotient construction

proof.text:
The compatible maps $V\to V^+\to P$ and $U^+\to V^+\to P$ descend to $S\to P$ and $T^+\to P$. Indeed [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] identifies $S$ with $V/R_V$ and $T^+$ with $U^+/R_+$, and the coequalizer property of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] applies to these relations. They agree on $T$, as is checked after its surjective etale cover $U$. The cartesian relation identifications from step 4 also show
$$S\times_P V^+\simeq V,\qquad T^+\times_P V^+\simeq U^+.$$
Here is the sheaf-level check: a section of either left side lifts etale locally to a section of its atlas $V$ or $U^+$ and an arrow of $R^+$ joining its image to the specified section of $V^+$. The source pullback of $R^+$ to that atlas is exactly $R_V$ or $R_+$ by step 4. Its target gives a section of the same atlas with the prescribed image. It is unique: two choices give a kernel-relation arrow mapping to the identity arrow of $R^+$, and the same cartesian identification forces the arrow to be the identity. These local sections consequently glue uniquely. This proves the displayed isomorphisms and identifies the projection maps.

source.place: Tag 07VX construction; Tag 07W1, equation-cube, cartesian side faces

proof.text: The pullback of $S\to P$ to its atlas $V^+\to P$ is the scheme thickening $V\to V^+$, by step 7. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] with this singleton atlas. Its statement concludes representability and closed immersion without assuming either in advance. To obtain the thickening assertion, identify $|S|$ with the quotient of $|V|$ by its atlas relation and $|P|$ with the quotient of $|V^+|$ by its atlas relation. The homeomorphisms $|V|=|V^+|$ and $|R_V|=|R^+|$ from the scheme thickenings identify the two equivalence relations and their quotient topologies. Thus $|S|\to|P|$ is a homeomorphism, as required.

Let $Q/B$ be an algebraic space and let $a:S\to Q$, $b:T^+\to Q$ agree on $T$. Restrict them to $V$ and $U^+$. Step 2 gives a unique $h:V^+\to Q$ extending both, because the scheme pushout also has space targets. The two composites $h s^+$ and $h t^+$ agree on $R_V$ (both are induced by $a$) and on $R_+$ (both are induced by $b$). Step 2 for the relation pushout makes them equal on $R^+$. The coequalizer assertion of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] gives a unique map $P\to Q$. Its restrictions are $a,b$, checked on the two atlases. Conversely every map $P\to Q$ gives that pair. Uniqueness follows first on $V^+$ and then on its quotient. Thus $P$ is the required pushout. When the starting objects are schemes, step 2 and uniqueness of a pushout identify it with their scheme pushout.

For the given arbitrary $X/S,Y/T^+$ and $\phi$, put $U_0=X\times_S T$ and use $\phi$ to identify it with $Y\times_{T^+}T$. The map $U_0\to Y$ is a thickening and $U_0\to X$ is affine: after any scheme test these are base changes of the corresponding original maps. Base change preserves the closed embedding and the nil defining ideal, and affineness follows by testing over affine schemes; the sheaf fibre products are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply the construction of steps 3--9 to this new diagram, obtaining $Z=X\amalg_{U_0}Y$. Its pushout property gives $Z\to P$ and the two canonical comparison maps. This application uses the existence already proved, rather than assuming the recovery conclusion.

source.place: Tag 07W0, construction of G on arbitrary compatible triples

proof.text: Choose a scheme $X_1$ with a representable surjective etale map to $X\times_S V$. Such an atlas exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Put $U_1=X_1\times_S T$. It is a scheme affine over $X_1$. Its map to $U_0\times_T U$ is surjective etale, as a base change of the chosen atlas. Regard $U_0\times_T U$ as the closed restriction of the space $Y\times_{T^+}U^+$. By [lem-sfb-space-thickening-etale-scheme-equivalence], $U_1$ lifts to a surjective etale scheme $Y_1\to Y\times_{T^+}U^+$, with its specified identification on the closed restriction; surjectivity follows from the same point-set argument as in step 3. Thus $(X_1,Y_1)$ is a compatible pair of scheme covers of $(X,Y)$, together with a compatible map to $(V,U^+)$. Form $W_1=X_1\amalg_{U_1}Y_1$. In the construction of $Z$ use precisely this atlas of $X$ and this lift to $Y$. Steps 6--7 applied to that construction give a surjective etale map $W_1\to Z$ and canonical identifications $X\times_Z W_1=X_1$ and $Y\times_Z W_1=Y_1$. The scheme pushout gives $W_1\to V^+$, and its composite to $P$ agrees with $W_1\to Z\to P$ by uniqueness on its two pieces.

source.place: Tag 07W0, the two atlas cubes (Tags 07W1 and 07W2)

proof.text:
Pull back $X\to Z\times_P S$ along the surjective etale cover $W_1\to Z$. Step 11 identifies its source with $X_1$. Steps 7 and 11 identify its target with
$$W_1\times_P S=W_1\times_{V^+}V.$$
Step 1, now for the compatible scheme triple $(X_1,Y_1)$ over the base scheme pushout $V^+=V\amalg_U U^+$, identifies this target with $X_1$ by exactly the canonical comparison. The pulled-back comparison is therefore an isomorphism. Likewise the pullback of $Y\to Z\times_P T^+$ has source $Y_1$ and target $W_1\times_{V^+}U^+\simeq Y_1$, again by the canonical comparison of step 1. These imply that the original two maps are isomorphisms: for a section of either target, lift its $Z$-coordinate to $W_1$ on an etale cover, use the indicated inverse there, and glue. The local inverses agree on overlaps because each inverts the same morphism; existence and uniqueness of this gluing are the sheaf axiom in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 07W0, final paragraph; explicit descent of the canonical comparisons

proof.text: Finally, the two maps just proved invertible are induced by the inclusions $X\to Z$ and $Y\to Z$. On $U_0=X\times_S T$, those inclusions agree after the given identification with $Y\times_{T^+}T$, by the defining pushout equation. Consequently their restrictions over $T$ identify the two recovered pieces by the specified $\phi$, not by an unspecified isomorphism. All auxiliary etaleness assumptions concern chosen atlases; no flatness or local finite presentation was imposed on $X$ or $Y$. The identity thickening, empty spaces and arbitrary locally nil ideals are included throughout.

lean.note: The three theorem signatures jointly give space-pushout existence and the thickening inclusion, existence of a scheme pushout which is also a space pushout, and canonical recovery of arbitrary compatible spaces. IsPullback expresses invertibility of each canonical comparison.
